title: Guided Notes

vocab.Observational study: A study in which you measure or survey a sample without trying to affect anyone. Nobody is assigned to a group --- the groups already exist. A survey is one type.
vocab.Explanatory variable: The variable we think might explain or account for the other one --- the tail of the arrow in the claim being tested.
vocab.Response variable: The variable we measure to see what happens --- the head of the arrow.
vocab.Association: Two variables move together: knowing which group an individual is in changes what you expect for the other variable. Not the same as causation.
vocab.Lurking variable: A variable outside the study that affects both variables in it, and can create an association all by itself.
